cases.name: Amy Lynn Fuller Mullis
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Amy was raised in the Eldora area and graduated from Eldora-New Providence High School in 1997.  She then graduated as an RN from Kirkwood Community College. Amy worked at St. Luke’s Hospital in Cedar Rapids and then in the ER at the Regional Medical Center in Manchester.  After the birth of her children, Amy chose to be a stay at home mom and partner in their farming operation. Amy was a member of the Delaware County Pork Producer’s Board.  She loved farming, hunting, fishing, and camping.  Amy also enjoyed gardening and was an avid Iowa Hawkeyes fan.  She liked designing and making t-shirts.  She was always there for her family and friends.  Above all else, Amy’s children were the most important part of her life."
cases.narrative:
On the day of her death, Amy and Todd had been working on their property with their son, Trysten. When Amy failed to return after being sent to get a pet carrier from the shed, Trysten went looking for her and found her on her hands and knees, face down, with the corn rake sticking out of her back.

The medical examiner ruled Amy’s death a homicide after noting that the corn rake had only four tines, but there were six puncture wounds in the victim’s back, as well as injuries to her chin, cheekbone, knees and knuckles. Assistant state medical examiner Dr. Kelly Kruse testified that the wound paths were consistent with her being impaled by the corn rake at least two, and possibly three, times.
